definition: In a way that is easy to see or notice, so that something stands out.
example: Her name was conspicuously absent from the list of volunteers thanked at the meeting.
nuance: Unlike ostentatiously, it doesn't mean someone is showing off. It means only that something stands out, and it is often used for an absence people notice.
prompt: A student arrives at a formal concert dressed very differently from everyone else.
options: In a bright orange tracksuit, he sat conspicuously among rows of dark suits and gowns.
Nobody spotted him all evening because he was dressed so conspicuously.
He had conspicuously read the dress code three times and followed every rule.
He silently wondered, conspicuously, whether anyone in the hall had noticed his outfit.
reasons: A vivid outfit in a sea of dark formal clothes is impossible to miss.
Whatever stands out gets noticed, so going unseen is the opposite.
Careful rule-following calls for the look-alike conscientiously, and it contradicts his unusual outfit.
An unspoken thought is hidden from others, so it cannot catch anyone's eye.

practice.prompt: Volunteers have just tidied a city park before a weekend festival.
options: The new benches were placed conspicuously behind a shed, where no visitor would find them.
The grass grew conspicuously, looking exactly like the grass in every other part of the park.
The organizers conspicuously suspected that raccoons had scattered the litter.
A single overflowing trash can stood conspicuously beside the freshly swept path.
reasons: Hiding something out of sight is the reverse of making it stand out.
Something identical to everything around it blends in rather than standing out.
The word isn't a substitute for suspiciously, and a private suspicion can't be seen.
One messy bin in an otherwise spotless park would draw every visitor's attention.
